title: No, Flock isn't threatening people for debating surveillance

paragraphs.text: Photos of purported cease and desist letters from the company have gone viral, but Flock says it didn’t send them.
paragraphs.translation: 網路上瘋傳幾張據稱是該公司寄出的「停止與終止函」照片，但 Flock 表示這些信並非該公司所發。

paragraphs.text: On Thursday, the Instagram account for a lecture series in Newport Beach, CA posted a photo of what appeared to be a cease and desist letter from the surveillance technology company Flock Safety. Flock has received significant backlash over its technology and work with law enforcement agencies, and this letter kicked off yet another wave of criticism against the company for allegedly trying to shut down discussions of its work.
paragraphs.translation: 週四，加州新港灘（Newport Beach）一個講座系列的 Instagram 帳號貼出一張照片，內容看似是監控科技公司 Flock Safety 寄出的停止與終止函。Flock 因其技術與和執法機關的合作關係已飽受抨擊，而這封信件又掀起新一波批評聲浪，指控該公司試圖打壓外界對其業務的討論。

paragraphs.text: “WE WILL NOT BE SILENCED,” the group, The Saturday Salon, wrote in the Instagram post, which has more than 3,000 likes. A separate post about the letter on Bluesky has more than 360 reposts. The text of the letter demands that the group stop hosting conversations about Flock’s surveillance technology. In a DM from The Saturday Salon’s Instagram account, Schuyler Lifschultz tells The Verge that it “found this letter taped to our front door.”
paragraphs.translation: 「我們不會被噤聲」，這個名為 The Saturday Salon 的團體在 Instagram 貼文中寫道，該貼文已獲得超過 3,000 個讚。Bluesky 上另一則關於此信件的貼文則有超過 360 次轉發。信件內容要求該團體停止舉辦討論 Flock 監控技術的活動。The Saturday Salon 的 Instagram 帳號透過私訊告訴《The Verge》，他們是「在自家前門發現這封被貼在門上的信」。

paragraphs.text: But Flock denies that it sent the letter, with chief strategy officer Rahul Sidhu citing it as an example of a mass disinformation campaign against Flock. “Flock never sent this letter, these people made it up (with a forged signature) to try to manipulate people,” Sidhu says. “We are pro-democracy. People SHOULD have discussions and lectures like this.”
paragraphs.translation: 但 Flock 否認曾寄出這封信，首席策略長 Rahul Sidhu 將此事視為針對 Flock 的大規模不實資訊操作案例之一。「Flock 從未寄出這封信，這些人是自己捏造出來的（還偽造了簽名），企圖操弄大眾，」Sidhu 表示。「我們支持民主。大家『應該』要有這樣的討論與講座。」

paragraphs.text: In a statement to The Verge, Flock’s chief legal officer, Dan Haley, says that Flock is aware of “at least two forged” letters and that “these letters did not come from me or from anyone at Flock.” Here is Haley’s full statement:
paragraphs.translation: Flock 的首席法務長 Dan Haley 在給《The Verge》的聲明中表示，Flock 已知悉「至少有兩封偽造」信件，並強調「這些信件並非出自我本人或 Flock 任何一位員工之手」。以下是 Haley 的完整聲明：

paragraphs.text: We’re aware of at least two forged letters circulating on the internet, including this one, that purport to be cease-and-desist letters from our legal department. To be clear: these letters did not come from me or from anyone at Flock. Flock welcomes and encourages public debate about our technology. We have not and would not seek to discourage, prevent, or prohibit such discussion and debate. In fact, we would be happy to participate in any such discussions the group in question might host in the future.
paragraphs.translation: 我們已知悉網路上至少流傳著兩封偽造信件，包括這一封，這些信件都自稱是我們法務部門發出的停止與終止函。在此澄清：這些信件並非出自我本人或 Flock 任何一位員工。 Flock 歡迎並鼓勵大眾就我們的技術展開公開辯論。我們從未、也不會試圖勸阻、阻止或禁止這類討論與辯論。事實上，若該團體未來舉辦類似討論活動，我們很樂意參與其中。

paragraphs.text: Looking closely at the photo of the letter in The Saturday Salon’s post reveals some dodgy details. Haley’s title in the letter is “Head of Legal Affairs Division,” but his actual title is chief legal officer. The Verge also emailed Haley’s purported email address on the letter but received a bounceback.
paragraphs.translation: 仔細檢視 The Saturday Salon 貼文中信件的照片，可以發現一些可疑的細節。信中列出的 Haley 職稱是「法務事務部主管」，但他實際的職稱是首席法務長。《The Verge》也試著寄信到信中列出的 Haley 電子郵件地址，結果收到退信通知。

paragraphs.text: Lifschultz tells The Verge that The Saturday Salon would “love to have somebody from Flock come in and tell their views and give a lecture. We are politically neutral and not a business.”
paragraphs.translation: Lifschultz 告訴《The Verge》，The Saturday Salon「很樂意邀請 Flock 的人來分享他們的看法、進行一場講座。我們在政治上保持中立，也不是一間營利事業」。

paragraphs.text: One of the other apparently forged letters Flock is aware of was shared in an Instagram post from musician Noah Orion. On his website, Orion has a shop listing for “Fuck Flock” stickers, and the cease and desist letter in the photo says that Orion has engaged in conduct “involving the unauthorized dissemination” of visual materials in a way that encourages Orion’s fans to “claim and place stickers that constitute a rude and unusual manner towards our company and association.”
paragraphs.translation: Flock 已知悉的另一封疑似偽造信件，是由音樂人 Noah Orion 在 Instagram 貼文中分享的。Orion 在自己的網站上販售「Fuck Flock」貼紙，而照片中的停止與終止函指控 Orion「未經授權散布」視覺素材，慫恿粉絲「索取並張貼對本公司及協會構成粗魯且異常方式的貼紙」。

paragraphs.text: This letter also has some unusual characteristics, such as identifying the company as Flock Cameras and Flock incorporated [sic]. The letter in the photo says that failure to comply with the purported cease and desist “may result in Flock Group inc. [sic] to persecute you”, which is both an awkwardly worded phrase and incorrectly uses “persecute” instead of “prosecute.” Orion didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
paragraphs.translation: 這封信也有一些不尋常之處，例如將公司名稱寫成「Flock Cameras」和「Flock incorporated」〔原文如此〕。照片中的信件寫道，若未遵守這份所謂的停止與終止函，「可能導致 Flock Group inc.〔原文如此〕對你進行 persecute（迫害）」，這句話不但用詞拗口，還誤用了「persecute（迫害）」一詞，正確用字應為「prosecute（起訴）」。Orion 並未立即回覆置評請求。

quiz.sentence_zh: 那份據稱的證據結果完全是捏造的。
